newsitem.title: CHINA: China convertible bonds limited to domestic buyers.
newsitem.headline: China convertible bonds limited to domestic buyers.

text.p: Convertible corporate bonds to be offered by Chinese companies initially will be limited to domestic investors, China Securities Regulatory Commission chairman Zhou Daojiong said on Wednesday.
Domestic companies would be allowed to issue convertible bonds, but on a trial basis, in the future, Zhou told reporters.
Last week, China announced regulations to allow companies to offer debt that could be converted into equity, with up to four billion yuan to be offered.
"We are doing this on a trial basis," Zhou said.
"If there are problems, only a few companies will be affected," he said, hinting that if the offers were not a success authorities may not approve the full four billion issue.
Listed companies would not be among those initially allowed to offer convertible debt.
Zhou said domestic institutions would be the likely investors in the first batch of convertible debt to be offered under the new rules.
"These will be for domestic investors," he said when asked if foreign investors would be allowed to buy.
If such offerings were successfully carried through, this form of raising capital might gain expanded use, he said.

China announced last week that some of China's top state enterprises could soon apply to issue convertible bonds, with a total value of four billion yuan ($481.9 billion), pushing them toward eventual listings on the stock market.
